
`Cannot find source file` seems to be coming from here:
https://github.com/webpack-contrib/source-map-loader/blob/v0.2.0/index.js#L65

I'm not too worried about that though because it just seems to be wrapping the underlying error which is:
```
Error: Can't resolve './https://raw.githubusercontent.com/japgolly/scalajs-react/v1.0.0-RC1/core/src/main/scala/japgolly/scalajs/react/CtorType.scala' in '/home/golly/projects/misc/target/scala-2.12/scalajs-bundler/main'
```

I submitted a PR to loader-utils to stop the prefixing, that's where that was happening:
https://github.com/webpack/loader-utils/pull/79

Unfortunately I'm still getting the same errors, just the prefix has been correctly removed:
```
Error: Can't resolve 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/japgolly/scalajs-react/v1.0.0-RC1/core/src/main/scala/japgolly/scalajs/react/internal/Semigroup.scala' in '/home/golly/projects/misc/target/scala-2.12/scalajs-bundler/main'
 @ ./target/scala-2.12/scalajs-bundler/main/fastopt-launcher.js 1:0-91
```

Looks like [scalajs-bundler is using the source-map-loader](https://github.com/scalacenter/scalajs-bundler/search?utf8=%E2%9C%93&q=source-map-loader&type=). The source-map-loader uses webpack's resolver to resolve the source-map. webpack's resolver, however, cannot resolve remote resources via http and such.

So, why are they using the source-map-loader at all?

And: I'm also not sure if it's a good idea to point the `sourceMappingURL` to `raw.githubusercontent.com`...

> So, why are they using the source-map-loader at all?

We use source-map-loader to preserve (as most as possible) source-map continuity across libraries.

issue.title: Avoid processing raw scala.js output using webpack
issue.body:
This PR basically merges the regular and reload workflows by avoiding running webpack on the scala.js output entirely.

What happens is that whenever the scala.js output file changes, we inspect the scala.js output via scala.js itself and determine all the imports it's making just like the reload workflow does. Then, instead of using that to construct a concatenated file, we use it to construct a replacement entry-point file for the main webpack process. This entry point is simply an object containing references to each of the dependencies used by the scala.js code and a simple require function that returns them.

We then run webpack in "library" mode, which gives us a handle to the produced blob. The end result is that we end up with 3 files:

1. The "library", which is an object containing references for each dependency referenced in the fastopt / opt file. There's no reason it couldn't support multiple entry-points if it doesn't already. The entrypoint file includes a trivial "require" implementation that simply returns the referenced element of the object, which is how we ensure that any css, html, text etc loaders work properly.
3.  The "loader". This is two lines of code. It creates the exports {} global for the module, and maps require from the library into the global namespace. I'd like to see if we can't incorporate this into the scala.js main wrapper or something and eliminate it.
5. The scala.js output file, in CommonJS format. It hooks into the exports and requires provided by the loader.

Finally, to produce the bundle, we concatenate the webpack output with the scala.js output file inside an IIFE and pull the require method into scope so the scala.js file can use it. I think we should consider deprecating this part entirely, as it doesn't play well with source-maps. I've fiddled around with the webpack concat-source-maps plugin but it just generates junk and frankly having two files performs better in the browser and will cache better.

This workflow definitely "works", and takes webpack times from 50+ seconds to 1 or 2 on my project. It also properly supports loaders such as html, raw, json, css and styles, and external webpack modules. 

There are a few other fixes mixed in here as well. They are separate commits and could be pulled forward.

- Add support for webpack 3 and change the default webpack version to 3.4.

There are still some refinements that can be made, including:

- Improve change detection. Right now it doesn't seem like changes to the webpack config force a rebuild, for instance, and changes to the fast-opt file that don't result in a new entry point cause webpack to re-run unnecessarily. Also, changes to .js resources don't seem to force a rebuild.

- What happens when .js code tries to import stuff from the scala.js file? I'm running scala code from the js side, but i'm not using es6 modules on the .js side.

- Investigate and adjust support for multiple entry points

- Investigate scala.js resource consolidation. As things stand, scala.js only copies .js files from the resources tree, which means you can't use things like angular templates or inline css. 

- Update documentation

- Add a -twirl subproject with a tag to add all the generated assets. I have the code for this, just need to set up the sbt bit.

- Make things work on windows. At least with my project the paths in the webpack file seem to get munged up.

issue.title: Source map URLs shouldn't be prefixed with a local path

repository.name: source-map-loader
repository.description: extract sourceMappingURL comments from modules and offer it to webpack

issue.body:
**Do you want to request a *feature* or report a *bug*?**

Bug.

**What is the current behavior?**

Some libraries (i.e. nearly all created via [Scala.JS](http://www.scala-js.org/)) have URLs in their source maps. However when being used with webpack, webpack is prepending a `./` to all the URLs results in trillions of warnings like this:

```
[info] Cannot find source file 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scala/scala/v2.12.1/src/library/scala/collection/immutable/Vector.scala': Error: Can't resolve './https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scala/scala/v2.12.1/src/library/scala/collection/immutable/Vector.scala' in '/home/golly/projects/misc/target/scala-2.12/scalajs-bundler/main'
[info]  @ ./fastopt-launcher.js 1:0-91
[info] 
[info] WARNING in ./demo-fastopt.js
[info] Cannot find source file 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scala/scala/v2.12.1/src/library/scala/collection/immutable/List.scala': Error: Can't resolve './https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scala/scala/v2.12.1/src/library/scala/collection/immutable/List.scala' in '/home/golly/projects/misc/target/scala-2.12/scalajs-bundler/main'
[info]  @ ./fastopt-launcher.js 1:0-91
[info] 
[info] WARNING in ./demo-fastopt.js
[info] Cannot find source file 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scala/scala/v2.12.1/src/library/scala/collection/immutable/Stream.scala': Error: Can't resolve './https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scala/scala/v2.12.1/src/library/scala/collection/immutable/Stream.scala' in '/home/golly/projects/misc/target/scala-2.12/scalajs-bundler/main'
[info]  @ ./fastopt-launcher.js 1:0-91
[info] 
[info] WARNING in ./demo-fastopt.js
[info] Cannot find source file 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scala/scala/v2.12.1/src/library/scala/collection/immutable/StringOps.scala': Error: Can't resolve './https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scala/scala/v2.12.1/src/library/scala/collection/immutable/StringOps.scala' in '/home/golly/projects/misc/target/scala-2.12/scalajs-bundler/main'
[info]  @ ./fastopt-launcher.js 1:0-91
[info] 
[info] WARNING in ./demo-fastopt.js
[info] Cannot find source file 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scala/scala/v2.12.1/src/library/scala/collection/immutable/WrappedString.scala': Error: Can't resolve './https://raw.githubusercontent.com/scala/scala/v2.12.1/src/library/scala/collection/immutable/WrappedString.scala' in '/home/golly/projects/misc/target/scala-2.12/scalajs-bundler/main'
[info]  @ ./fastopt-launcher.js 1:0-91
```

And resulting in a final source map that no longer works for those libraries.

**If the current behavior is a bug, please provide the steps to reproduce.**

Setup any dummy project with [Scala.JS](http://www.scala-js.org/) and [scalajs-bundler](https://scalacenter.github.io/scalajs-bundler/getting-started.html) which runs everything through webpack.

**What is the expected behavior?**

Source map links that can be identified as absolute URLs should be used as is, without modification.

I believe the fix would be a very simple test like this before prepending:
https://github.com/jantimon/html-webpack-plugin/pull/619/files

**Please mention other relevant information such as the browser version, Node.js version, webpack version and Operating System.**

Using webpack 2.2.1, Node.JS 7.7.3.
